messages:
sre-oncall: fyi seeing apiserver read p95 spike in eu-central1 since 10:10UTC, ctrlmgr leader flips ~20-30s. gpu provisioning queue climbing.

anil: checking etcd nodes and disk I/O.

maria: nvme hosts reporting fsync delays and blk errors; sample: 
`blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1`

chris: gpu-provisioner backlog ~1500, provision rate dropped from ~40/s to ~9/s.

infra-bot: ALERT apiserver_read_latency_p95 eu-central1 triggered

anil: likely WAL fsync stalls -> apiserver timeouts -> ctrlmgr lease fails.

maria: ctrlmgr log: "failed to renew lease: operation timed out"

chris: mitigation options: throttle onboarding, divert to west-eu, bump etcd fsync retry/backoff, increase controller leader timeouts.

sre-oncall: do quick mitigations: anil/maria bump etcd WAL retry backoff and increase leader-election durations. chris prepare west-eu diversion. I'll send customer note.

anil: applied etcd WAL backoff change and cordoned one NVMe host for healthcheck.

maria: increasing ctrlmgr lease duration to 60s and renew deadline to 40s; doing staggered restarts.

chris: labeling eu-central nodes provisioning=lowprio and spinning 5-node west-eu canary now.

sre-oncall: monitoring p95. if re-spike -> incident. post-mit: NVMe firmware check, consider higher-iops etcd leaders, add admission rate-limit for bursty gpu requests, cost analysis for diversion.

maria: opening follow-up ticket and assigning owners.

sre-oncall: thanks team.
